title: CopperMCP DRC Summary

passed.description: Hard gate: true when KiCad reported no error-severity violation and no unconnected item. Warnings and exclusions are permitted, because KiCad treats them as non-blocking.
passed.$comment: Derived from error_count and unconnected_count. Published rather than left to the caller so every consumer applies the same gate.

clean.description: Stricter presentation signal: true only when the report carries no findings and no ignored checks at all. A warning-only board is passed but not clean.
clean.$comment: Derived from the five counts and violation_type_counts. Published rather than left to the caller so a warning-only report can never be re-derived as clean by a consumer that forgets ignored_check_count.

$comment: `passed` and `clean` are derived from the counts above, so the schema pins the derivation in both directions rather than declaring two free booleans. Without these, a payload could claim `clean: true` beside a nonzero count and still validate — a false claim about a board, reachable through the published contract, which the runtime model and the closed MCP contract both refuse. Not expressible here: the model also requires the violation-type counts to sum to error + warning + exclusion + unconnected, and JSON Schema has no arithmetic over sibling values.

allOf.title: passed is true exactly when there is no error and nothing unconnected
clean is true exactly when there is no finding and no ignored check at all
